text:
Alex: Heads-up — planning to enforce SSE-KMS for S3 object uploads + DB backup archives starting Friday. Need RBAC, audit additions, perf tests, and vuln triage signoff.
Mira: Is this a global enforcement or per-tenant opt-in?
Alex: Global by default; support can request an escape for legacy tenants. Goal: ensure nothing is stored at rest unencrypted.
Jordan: Main concern: KMS request quota. Re-encrypting an entire archive fleet could spike GenerateDataKey calls and throttle. We'll need throughput plan and retries.
Lee: Also discovered backup-agent v2.1.2 leaves plaintext temp files under /var/tmp during chunking in staging. Tagging @Mira for vuln triage and emergency patching.
Mira: Confirmed. There's a fix in PR #478 that switches to secure tempfile + shred. Recommend we block < v2.1.3 from uploading to prod.
Mira: snippet of fix:
```bash
# old behaviour
cat > /var/tmp/backup-chunk.tmp
# new behaviour
TMP=$(mktemp --tmpdir backup-XXXXXX)
# write to $TMP then shred -u $TMP
```
Jordan: For RBAC, we need a role that grants the agent PutObject plus KMS GenerateDataKey permissions. Rough IAM snippet: 
```json
{
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups/*","arn:aws:kms:...:key/EXAMPLE"]
}
```
Lee: Audit logging changes: add encryption_scheme (sse-kms|sse-s3|client-side), cmk_alias, cmk_keyid, uploader_principal, source_ip, bucket, object_size, and a boolean reencrypt_performed. We should feed these into auditbeat -> es with 30d retention.
Alex: Agreed. Also propose an async "re-encryptor" job that runs in the maintenance window to pick up legacy unencrypted objects and re-encrypt them server-side. Canary it on a subset first.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled Friday 02:00 UTC to prod-ops (note: automation alert).
Mira: Perf notes — SSE-KMS adds ~25–40ms per PUT for GenerateDataKey. For large multipart uploads the overhead is amortized, but high QPS small-object workloads will see latency/cost impact. Suggest envelope key caching per session to reduce KMS calls.
Jordan: KMS quotas again: ephemeral grants might help for hot paths (avoid repeated GenerateDataKey). Test plan: simulate 2k concurrent multipart uploads covering typical backup sizes and measure KMS throttle behaviour.
Lee: On vuln triage: if we revoke old agent versions we must ensure restore paths still work for customers on older clients. Need migration tooling and clear support docs.
Samir: Quick question — will DB backups use the same CMK as S3 backups? Mixing keys complicates restore and access grants.
Alex: Proposal: prefer tenant-specific CMKs for DB backups where available; otherwise use the global backups CMK. Document fallback order in runbook and include key id in backup metadata to make restores deterministic.
Mira: I'll merge the temp-file fix, open a blocker to block uploads from < v2.1.3, and create PR for audit schema changes.
Jordan: I'll schedule the load test for Thu 18:00 UTC, will post results and KMS metrics.
Lee: I'll update the log schema and retention policy, and add an alert if re-encryptor job error rate > 1%.
Alex: Action items summarized: (1) Security: revoke legacy agent uploads + patch rollout, (2) Infra: KMS throughput runbook + quota request, (3) Ops: implement canary re-encryptor job + sampling test, (4) Product/Support: opt-out ticket flow + restore migration docs. I'll file JIRA and link here.
Mira: ACK — linking PR #478 and JIRA BACKUP-1123 in a follow-up message.
Jordan: ACK — will post load test artifacts and ksm (sic) error traces.
Lee: ACK — will add audit mapping to the schema PR.
Samir: Thanks, looping in compliance to approve retention extension for these audit fields.
ops-bot: incident-bot: reminder: maintenance window Fri 02:00–04:00 UTC for canary.
